title: VI and Thermal Recovery in Landslide Areas: data and code

creators.name: Hsu, Yu-Chun
creators.affiliation: Department of Forestry, National Chung Hsing University; Innovation and Development Center of Sustainable Agriculture (SMARTer), Taichung, Taiwan

description:
Pipeline and model-ready data for a satellite-scale test of whether land surface temperature (LST) recovers as fast as greenness after forest disturbance in the montane forests of Taiwan.

Every estimate is defined as a disturbed patch minus terrain-matched intact forest within the same summer composite, so interannual climate and long-term warming cancel in the difference. Fourteen Landsat 8/9 summer composites (2013-2026, 792 scenes) and Taiwan's official event-based landslide catalogue give 23,526 disturbed patches. Intact canopy cools summer daytime LST by 0.48 +/- 0.03 °C per additional 10 m of height and saturates above 30 m. The net thermal shock is +0.82 to +2.31 °C in the well-sampled cohorts. Thermal recovery is slower than greenness recovery, tau_LST 16.8 yr against tau_NDVI 14.7 yr, a ratio of 1.15 (95% CI 1.09-1.20) whose point estimate is above one in every fitted stratum; 74% of the pooled thermal decline is reproduced within patches. The lag scales with scar size, from a ratio of 1.05 below 2 ha, where the two clocks are inseparable, to 1.45 above 10 ha. The tau ratio is the quotient of the two fitted tau; the patch-level bootstrap supplies its interval.

This deposit holds the analysis pipeline and the point and tabular data extracted from the source datasets, with every coordinate column removed. reproduce.py rebuilds every reported statistic from those tables in the order of the paper's Methods section and compares each regenerated result file with the released copy, key by key. No figure scripts are included. No satellite imagery and no rendered figures are included; each source archive is documented in the README and in outputs/DATA_PROVENANCE.json with access URLs, retrieval times and file checksums. The event-based landslide catalogue is not redistributed, because redistribution rights do not belong to this study.
